haiku-low.q1: If reports.row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the API streams the CSV in the response. Larger reports return 202 with export id and status; a background job builds the file and emails a 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: The API returns the existing queued or running export with 202 and starts no new job. The duplicate check ignores filters, so the page shows the old filters.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. No code deletes export files, and unfinished uploads are discarded after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with waits of 60 and 300 seconds. After the third failure, on_final_failure sets the row to failed and the user gets a failure email.
haiku-low.q5: Only the read replica. Report rows are never read from the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row's status column. The page calls GET .../exports/latest on load and polls every 5 seconds while queued or running.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 500-row pages by row_id and writes CSV into one roughly 8 MB buffer, uploading each full buffer as a multipart part. Only one buffer is in memory, so the report is never held whole.
haiku-low.q8: On error the upload is aborted, so the written parts are discarded. After a timeout or worker death, the unfinished upload stays until the bucket discards it after 24 hours. Each attempt restarts from the first row in a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: Captured in the URL and saved in the query column of the report_exports row. The job payload holds only the export id, and the job reads the query from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on report_exports covering queued or running rows for the same user and report. A second simultaneous insert is rejected and the existing row is returned.
haiku-low.q11: The upload must have completed at its key and the row set to done with object_key. A rerun on a done or failed row stops at the check, so no rebuild and no second email.
haiku-low.q12: The user receives a partial file download and must click Download CSV again. No retry or cleanup is described for the small path.

sonnet.q1: Step 1 reads reports.row_count (not filtered, up to a day old). 10,000 rows or fewer: small path, response streams the CSV (header row first, columns in URL order), nothing stored, no job. More than 10,000: large path, quick 202 reply with export id and status; a background job builds the CSV in object storage and emails a 24-hour link.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index rejects the insert. The API returns the existing queued/running row with 202 and starts no new job. Filters are ignored in this check, so the page may show the old filters.
sonnet.q3: The emailed signed link works for 24 hours. No code deletes files; the bucket lifecycle rule deletes each file 7 days after creation. (The page's status call issues a new 24-hour link while done, until the file is gone.)
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts total (waits of 60 s before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3). After the third failure the queue calls on_final_failure once, which sets the row to failed and sends the failure email. The page shows failed; earlier failures send no email.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only, never the primary database, for both the small and large paths.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table row (status queued/running/done/failed). The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load, so a returning user sees the state, and polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping at done or failed. When done, the response includes a fresh 24-hour signed link.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads the replica in 500-row pages by row_id, writes CSV into one ~8 MB buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, and holds only one buffer in memory at a time. It completes the upload at the end so the file appears at its key.
sonnet.q8: On an error, the job aborts the upload and raises, so parts are discarded. On a timeout or worker death nothing cleans up; the unfinished upload stays until the bucket discards it after 24 hours. Nothing is downloadable since the upload was never completed. The next attempt restarts from the beginning (first row, new multipart upload) because the queue keeps no progress.
sonnet.q9: Saved in the query column of the report_exports row, not in the job payload. The payload contains only the export id, and the job loads the row to read the query.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on report_exports (condition: status queued or running, one per user per report). It stops two simultaneous clicks from both inserting.
sonnet.q11: The upload must have been completed (file downloadable at its key), and the row set to done with object_key and finished_at; only then send_email is called with the signed link. If the job is run again and the row is already done or failed, it stops and does nothing: no rebuild, no second email.
sonnet.q12: The user gets a partial file and clicks again. Nothing is stored and no job runs. The stream must finish within the API's 60-second limit.
